question: What is the key advantage of the hybrid deployment model over fully self-hosted?
options: Hybrid provides better audio quality than self-hosted
Hybrid deployments are required for HIPAA compliance
Hybrid lets LiveKit Cloud handle WebRTC infrastructure (the hardest part) while your agent runs on your own infrastructure with direct access to internal systems behind your firewall
Hybrid is always cheaper than self-hosted at scale
explanation: The hybrid model splits responsibility: LiveKit Cloud manages the complex WebRTC infrastructure (SFU routing, global edge, TURN, TLS) while your agent workers run inside your network. This means direct access to databases, CRMs, and internal APIs without exposing them to the internet, and without needing WebRTC expertise on your team.

question: Why is agent code portable across all three deployment models (Cloud, self-hosted, hybrid)?
options: The agent logic is the same regardless of where it runs — only the deployment configuration (how the agent connects to LiveKit) changes between models
LiveKit provides a compatibility layer that translates between deployment models
Each model uses the same Docker base image
All three models use identical Kubernetes configurations
explanation: Your agent code interacts with the LiveKit SDK the same way regardless of deployment model. Whether the LiveKit server is managed Cloud infrastructure, your own Kubernetes cluster, or a hybrid setup, the agent connects via the same URL and API keys. Only the deployment wrapper — how you configure and run the container — differs.

question: When evaluating deployment models, why should team capacity be considered alongside technical requirements?
options: Larger teams always prefer self-hosted deployments
Cloud deployments require larger teams than self-hosted
Self-hosting requires WebRTC expertise, Kubernetes operations, and on-call coverage — if the team lacks these skills, Cloud or hybrid avoids a significant operational burden
Team capacity only matters for the initial setup, not ongoing operations
explanation: Self-hosting LiveKit is a significant operational commitment: WebRTC networking, Kubernetes management, scaling policies, monitoring, and on-call coverage. Without dedicated infrastructure expertise, the team will struggle with reliability. Cloud or hybrid lets a small team focus on agent quality rather than infrastructure operations.
